uncited: *   **Input:** A pre-trained Instant-NGP NeRF representation (hashgrid), a user-defined cage mesh surrounding the target object, and user interactions (cage vertex displacements).
*   **Output:** A modified NeRF representation where the selected object is deformed according to the cage, with artifacts reduced by volumetric membrane interpolation.
The grid stores feature vectors for each active voxel.
The user selects an object using a scribble-based interface.
For each sample point $x$ along a ray, the method computes its position relative to the cage.
*   Let $\hat{v}_i$ be the displaced positions of the cage vertices (modified by the user).
A technique where a bounding mesh (cage) is manipulated to deform the enclosed volume.
It is chosen for its intuitive control and suitability for volumetric data. [Link to Cage-Based Deformation](#)
The use of a trainable sparse occupancy grid queried via CUDA kernels.
It is chosen for its speed and interactive performance. [Link to Instant-NGP](#)
A post-processing step inspired by Poisson Image Editing to smooth artifacts.
It is chosen when geometric edits introduce discontinuities. [Link to Membrane Interpolation](#)
*   **When to use:** When interactive, real-time editing of existing NeRF geometry is required.
*   **When not to use:** When inpainting missing regions or generating new content is required.
